Minding the Agents

Building Harnesses for Scientific Reporting

Andriy Koval

2026-07-13

(A) Starting thoughts

As we approach designing harnesses for scientific reporting, let us consider principles that could guide our thinking.

A1 The harness we build is an expression of the objectives we perceive.

A2 Agent exists to help you pay attention, to guide your focus.

A3 With language we inject our mind into files.

A1 Reflection and Expression

A1 The harness we build is an expression of the objectives we perceive.

Reflection — skills and templates will be shaped by our mental models and cognitive habits, intended or not

Expression — skills and templates should therefore be built to express opinions, not merely to execute tasks

Each script is unique, but united by a common structure.

Genres, styles, compositional conventions and techniques

Generic fugal structure — composerfocus.com

A2 Focus and Learning

A2 Agent exists to help you pay attention, to guide your focus.

Ramifications of this principle for harness design:

  • The shape of the harness is meant for humans
  • Human learning is agent’s success criterion

A3 Words and Images

A3 With language we inject our mind into files.

(B) Scientific Reporting

Three territories of the reporting workflow, each solving a distinct problem.

B1 Manipulation — Raw data arrives in the shape of its source, not of our question; ./manipulation is where we reshape it and earn a trustworthy rectangle.

B2 Analysis — Data does not speak on its own; ./analysis is where we compose and catalogue the artifacts created during interrogation.

B3 Frontend — Some reports will never face external readers; ./_frontend-N is where we decide what to show, to whom, and how.

B1 ./manipulation

The rectangle we need is never the rectangle we are given. Manipulation is where we earn it.

Representative issues and challenges:

Grain confusion — two tables joined at different levels of aggregation silently inflate counts; always state the unit before the join

Universe filters — some questions are asked only of a subset; applying analysis to the full sample treats non-answers as implicit responses

Naming drift — the same concept is spelled differently across sources or vintages; a rename script quietly forks the schema

Label–value mismatch — factor labels in the codebook do not match the stored codes; recoding from memory rather than the codebook corrupts the variable

B2 ./analysis

A clean rectangle is silent. Analysis is where we build the instruments that make it speak.

Scope discipline — one folder holds one monothematic engagement, not a drawer of everything

Provenance — every derived table and figure traces back to a documented source column, not to memory

Variation is evidence — alternate cuts of the same question are siblings, not replacements; the discarded view stays part of the record

A scratch pad is not a report — until it renders, it does not exist

Genre shapes expectation — each engagement belongs to a recognizable form: exploratory (EDA), inferential (model estimation), or presentational (report)

B3 _frontend-*

A repository is not an argument. The frontend is where we choose the reader, and answer for the choice.B

Exposure — private paths, credentials, and working notes must not survive the trip to a public artifact

Register — a filename or a command is meaningful to an engineer and noise to an external reader

Custody — a document copied verbatim must arrive unedited, or the site must say plainly that it did not

Assembly — many independently authored reports must appear under one coherent navigation without being rewritten

Self-containment — a published page owns its own assets, or it rots the moment the source repository moves

(C) Agent Harnesses

Pipeline Orchestra

Engineering: raw data → trustworthy rectangle

Agent @pipeline-engineer

Writes to manipulation/

Flow source → ferry → ellis → served

Governs transport, transformation, and validation of incoming data

Accountability INPUT-manifest records what arrived; CACHE-manifest records what is served

Composing Orchestra

Reporting: clean data → analytical artifact

Agent @report-composer

Writes to analysis/

Flow contract → .R laboratory → .qmd publication

Governs monothematic engagement: one question, one folder, one artifact family

Accountability report-contract anchors scope; artifacts are numbered and inventoried

Publishing Orchestra

Publishing: existing artifacts → curated site

Agents @interviewer + @writer

Writes to _frontend-N/

Flow RAW → EDITED (content/) → PRINTED (_site/)

Governs editorial selection, audience register, and protocol fidelity

Accountability TRANSFORM_LOG records every change; fidelity report is the gate

C1 Pipeline Orchestra

Procedures and conventions for extracting, transporting, and transforming raw data

General form could be expressed as:

Script           ferry        ellis
Data      Source ----> Staged ----> Served
Manifest         INPUT        CACHE
But specific implementation will reflect the complexity of each project

C2 Composing Orchestra

                 └─ g12        └─ facet by age

                 └─ g22

  g = graph   t = table   fig = figure   out = output
